name: Annotated type-scale ramp with highlighted leading
looks: A row of the same glyph grows step by step across a scale, each step's size label ticking up beneath it, ending on one large instance. A second beat highlights a paragraph and a headline with teal measurement bands across every line, then a one-line code snippet typing on in a dark pill names the rule that produced them.
build: The glyph row scales each instance up from the last on a stagger (annotated-diagram-overlay's label pattern, applied to a size ramp instead of an arrow). The measurement bands are absolutely positioned rules that fade/scale in per line of text, synced to the text's own reveal; the code pill types on with terminal-type-on.
sound: A tick per glyph step, then a soft tick per measurement band, and a key tick under the code line.
prompt: Prove an invisible design rule with two linked beats: first a scale of the same element growing step by step with its values labelled, then a block of real text with its measurement called out line by line in an accent colour, finishing on the one line of code that defines the rule.
